hints.title: Track Consecutive Match Order
hints.text: Assign row numbers to all matches for each player ordered chronologically by match day.

hints.title: Isolate Winning Matches
hints.text: Filter winning matches and assign a second row number partitioned by player.

hints.title: Gaps and Islands Difference
hints.text: Subtract the winning row number from the overall row number to create a grouping key for consecutive wins.

hints.title: Complete SQL Query
hints.text:
```sql
WITH RankedMatches AS (
    SELECT 
        player_id,
        match_day,
        result,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY player_id ORDER BY match_day) AS overall_rn
    FROM Matches
),
WinMatches AS (
    SELECT 
        player_id,
        overall_rn,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY player_id ORDER BY match_day) AS win_rn
    FROM RankedMatches
    WHERE result = 'Win'
),
Streaks AS (
    SELECT 
        player_id,
        COUNT(*) AS streak
    FROM WinMatches
    GROUP BY player_id, (overall_rn - win_rn)
),
MaxStreaks AS (
    SELECT 
        player_id,
        MAX(streak) AS longest_streak
    FROM Streaks
    GROUP BY player_id
)
SELECT 
    p.player_id,
    COALESCE(m.longest_streak, 0) AS longest_streak
FROM (SELECT DISTINCT player_id FROM Matches) p
LEFT JOIN MaxStreaks m ON p.player_id = m.player_id;
```

complexity.time: O(N log N) window function sorting over match dates
variables: N: number of matches in Matches table
complexity.notes: Gaps-and-islands grouping via row number differences.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Self-joins over unbounded streaks produce exponential Cartesian products.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Row number differences group contiguous matches in a single window pass.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Apply the standard gaps-and-islands row number difference technique.

solutions.code:
import pandas as pd

def longest_winning_streak(matches: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    if matches.empty:
        return pd.DataFrame({'player_id': [], 'longest_streak': []})
    matches = matches.sort_values(['player_id', 'match_day']).copy()
    matches['overall_rn'] = matches.groupby('player_id').cumcount() + 1
    wins = matches[matches['result'] == 'Win'].copy()
    if wins.empty:
        res = pd.DataFrame({'player_id': matches['player_id'].unique()})
        res['longest_streak'] = 0
        return res
    wins['win_rn'] = wins.groupby('player_id').cumcount() + 1
    wins['grp'] = wins['overall_rn'] - wins['win_rn']
    streaks = wins.groupby(['player_id', 'grp']).size().reset_index(name='streak')
    max_streaks = streaks.groupby('player_id')['streak'].max().reset_index(name='longest_streak')
    all_players = pd.DataFrame({'player_id': matches['player_id'].unique()})
    res = all_players.merge(max_streaks, on='player_id', how='left')
    res['longest_streak'] = res['longest_streak'].fillna(0).astype(int)
    return res
solutions.approach: Pandas cumulative counts and groupby solution.
